summary: CPU investigation (no GPU) of the cat10 root-branch issue, prep for the post-22-flip-fix work: WHY does adding the depth-0 root sibling rescue d0 (+5) yet DILUTE d1-d4 (-28 net)? Reconcile with the proven alt-free drafter. Pin the d0-rescue rate + the dilution mechanism (m1 verify co-residency vs m3 commit-handoff vs trajectory artifact) from the saved cat10 data + the code. Design how to get the root d0 chance WITHOUT the -28, shape fixed = caterpillar + one root branch.

reads.mechanismRanked:
RANKED for the -28 (accept/event 3.1983→2.9316, -0.2667; saved output/fr13_cat10/{cat9,cat10}/accept_speed.json + metrics_final.txt):

RANK 1 = ARTIFACT (trajectory/denominator confound) — DOMINANT, partially decomposes the others.
Evidence: cat9 and cat10 produce DIFFERENT greedy streams that diverge EARLY — first-divergence pos {p0:17, p1:11, p2:21, p3:61} (computed from served_ids in accept_speed.json reps[0]). Once diverged, every downstream per-depth event is measured over a DIFFERENT token context. The smoking gun is prompt 0: cat10 served only 73 tokens vs cat9's 98 (served_lens [73,128,128,128] vs [98,128,128,128]) — cat10's p0 hit <|im_end|> EOS early (capture.json p0 ends at the im_end flip, flips_vs_oracle cat10 p0 pos72 served '<|im_end|>'). Net: cat10 made 25 FEWER tokens (457 vs 482) in 1 MORE event (117 vs 116), which MECHANICALLY lowers accept/event (more events producing fewer tokens). This is exactly playbook class 12 (per-depth numbers are RATES; whole-window accept is trajectory-confounded) and the BIND's own AXIS-2 caveat ("Whole-window accept/event is TRAJECTORY-CONFOUNDED ... each arm generated a different greedy stream").

RANK 2 = m3 (branch-commit state handoff) — a REAL but SMALL structural contributor, bounded.
Mechanism in code: committer is LCP-max (fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:5624-5648 best_lcp loop). The root sibling node 2 (1,) is its own leaf with parent=0 (computed parent array cat10 = [-1,0,0,1,1,3,3,5,5,7,7]); it can win ONLY when the spine's d0 (node1) is REJECTED and the sibling matches at d0 → best_path=[0,2], best_lcp=1, a STOP-AT-d0 commit that adds to the d0 per-pos counter but contributes 0 to d1+. The next event's conv-prior window + h0 then start from the accepted path's LEAF NODE column (accepted_paths[b,len-1], :1527-1530) = node 2's off-spine state. So sibling-wins both (a) inflate d0 while capping that event at d0, and (b) hand an off-spine state to the next rollout. BUT bounded SMALL: the rescue is only +5 d0 accepts/rep (101→106; +25 over full run 505→530); and a sibling commit has accepted_len=1 (num_accepted=1), so the documented conv prior-window bug (which fires at num_accepted>1, project_fr13_conv_priorwindow_root) does NOT trigger on sibling-stops — the handoff degradation channel is largely inert here.

RANK 3 = m1 (10-row verify-forward co-residency) — STRUCTURALLY WEAKENED, residual only.
Evidence AGAINST a large m1: the verify strict_mask (:233-241) is built by walking parent[] to root, so each row sees ONLY its strict ancestors; node 2 (1,) is never a parent of any spine node, so NO spine row has strict[spine,2]=1 — the root-sibling row is attention-invisible to every spine row, and the GDN tree scan uses the SAME strict_mask (:4111). So neither attention nor the recurrent accumulation can read the sibling's value. Residual m1 channel = fp reduction-order: kernel is called n_actual=tree_n (10 vs 11) with n_pad=tree_n_pad (BOTH pad to 16: cat9 n=10→16, cat10 n=11→16, via n_pad=1<<(n-1).bit_length() :227). The extra real row inside the same 16-pad tile CAN perturb the spine rows' fp accumulation IF the scan reduction is N-actual-dependent (the campaign's open seam: GDN scan num_warps=8/BV=16). This is the only physically-possible m1 leak and it is sub-ULP-scale, not -0.27.
reads.perDepthRealOrConfound:
CONFOUNDED at the whole-window level, but a REAL within-event signal survives when you condition. Decomposition (from per_depth_accept_count in accept_speed.json reps[0], cross-checked against metrics_final.txt full-run counters — identical conditionals):

MARGINAL rate (denom = ALL events, which is how measure_accept_speed.py:140 computes per_depth_accept_rate = per_pos[k]/d_drafts) drops at d1-d4: d1 0.828→0.727, d2 0.638→0.564, d3 0.483→0.419, d4 0.379→0.316. But the marginal is contaminated two ways: (i) the +1 event and -25 tokens trajectory confound, (ii) the d0 rescue means more events reach d0 but a fraction (sibling-stops) cap there, shrinking the d1+ population.

CONDITIONAL P(accept dK | accepted d(K-1)) = count[k]/count[k-1] REMOVES the denominator confound and is the fair read. cat9→cat10: d0 0.871→0.906 (+0.035), d1 0.951→0.802 (−0.149), d2 0.771→0.777 (+0.006 FLAT), d3 0.757→0.742 (−0.015), d4 0.786→0.755 (−0.031). THE DILUTION IS NOT DIFFUSE ACROSS d1-d4 — it is a SINGLE SHARP DROP at the d0→d1 transition (−0.149); d2/d3/d4 conditionals are essentially unchanged between arms. That d0→d1 concentration is the real, non-confounded signal: it is exactly where the root-sibling structure acts (sibling-stops remove d0-accepting events from the d1 population) AND where any trajectory-divergence first bites (streams diverge near d0). A pure sibling-stop model predicts d1≈96 (101 spine-d0 × 0.95) but observed d1=85, so ~11 of the d1 absolute drop (96→85) is NOT explained by sibling-stop structure alone → it is trajectory divergence (different contexts) plus at most a residual verify-forward d1 degradation. NET: the per-depth drop is REAL as a within-event d0→d1 effect but the d2-d4 'drops' are denominator/trajectory artifacts (conditionals flat).

Every sibling-win is a d0 accept that would otherwise have been a d0 REJECT (sibling can only fire when spine-d0 missed) — so the count of sibling-commit events is AT MOST the d0-rescue delta (~5/rep, ~25/full-run) and AT LEAST 0. The greedy-rescue definition (P(target==root-rank-2 | root-rank-1 missed), user-confirmed 86a255a4) means sibling-wins ⊆ {events where spine-d0 missed}; the measured +5 d0 accepts is the realized rescue. These ~5 sibling-stop events feed the m3 handoff but, being accepted_len=1 (num_accepted=1), do NOT trip the num_accepted>1 conv prior-window bug, so their handoff cost is bounded small. reads.flipAccretionCovary: DOES NOT CO-VARY — the flip redistribution and the accept drop are SEPARATE phenomena, both downstream of trajectory divergence rather than a single shared mechanism. Hard evidence: the cat9 flip set [6,6,4,6]=22 and cat10 flip set [2,6,8,6]=22 are 100% DISJOINT — zero overlapping (prompt_id,pos) pairs (computed from all_clear_margin_flips in both flips_vs_oracle.json; overlap = empty set). The total is FLAT (22=22, BIND AXIS-1 table). The flips land at entirely different positions because the two arms generate different streams (cat9 p0 flips at pos 69-97; cat10 p0 flips at pos 58,72 — the cat10 p0 EOS-early at 72 truncates the window). Even the 'known deep-row' flips diverge: p2_code_vs_files present in cat9, ABSENT in cat10 (because cat10's p2 stream diverged at pos21 and never hit that context); p3_Let_vs_codefence present in both. So the flip count is constant (the verify-forward GDN argmax defect, the 22, is independent of cat9-vs-cat10 — it is the SAME unfixed channel-2 defect, FR13_FLIP_DRAFTER_CAMPAIGN FINDING 1); only its POSITIONAL realization is reshuffled by the trajectory. The accept −0.27 is a separate trajectory+structural effect. They do NOT share a mechanism, so fixing the 22-flip verifier defect will NOT by itself remove the cat10 dilution, and vice-versa.
reads.forceSpinePrediction:
FR13_FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT (the override at :5675-5681 that forces best_path=spine_path's own lcp, scoring alts but never letting them win) is the m1-vs-m3 discriminator. PREDICTIONS:

If m3 (commit-handoff) is the carrier: forcing the spine commit removes all root-sibling wins → the off-spine state handoff never happens → the deep-spine (d1-d4) conditional acceptance RECOVERS toward cat9 (the d1 conditional 0.802 should climb back near 0.951), and the d0 rescue DISAPPEARS (d0 back to ~0.871, since the sibling can no longer win d0). Net: accept/event recovers toward 3.198 by losing the +5 rescue but regaining the deep-spine yield.

If m1 (10-row verify co-residency) is the carrier: forcing the spine commit changes only WHICH path commits, NOT the 10/11-row verify FORWARD shape (all rows are still computed and scored; force-spine only re-picks the winner). So the verify-forward fp reduction over the 11-row/16-pad tile is unchanged → the deep-spine per-event acceptance does NOT recover (d1 stays ~0.802). Net: persists.

CRUCIAL CAVEAT the CPU pass exposes: because the streams DIVERGE (artifact), a clean force-spine A/B MUST be run with cat10's drafter topology on cat10's OWN trajectory, comparing force-spine-ON vs OFF within the SAME boot/seed and measuring the CONDITIONAL P(d1|d0) (not whole-window accept). Otherwise the trajectory confound (the dominant rank-1 effect) will swamp the m1/m3 signal exactly as it does in the cat9-vs-cat10 comparison. Given the strict-mask isolation already proven on CPU (m1 largely impossible structurally) plus the conditional drop being concentrated precisely at d0→d1 (where sibling-stops act), the CPU evidence PREDICTS the force-spine boot will show RECOVERY → m3-leaning, but with a large residual that is trajectory-artifact, not a true per-event deep-spine degradation. The deferred boot should also dump FR10_METRICS to finally COUNT sibling-wins (the data this CPU pass could not recover).

reads.d0RescueRate:
d0-RESCUE RATE DECOMPOSED (aggregate vLLM per-pos counters, output/fr13_cat10/{cat9,cat10}/metrics_final.txt, cross-checks the per-rep accept_speed.json exactly):

cat9:  pos0 accept 505 / 580 drafts = d0 rate 0.8707 -> 75 root-rank-1 misses (12.93%)
cat10: pos0 accept 530 / 585 drafts = d0 rate 0.9060 -> 55 d0-rejects (9.40%)
d0 rate delta = +0.0353 (matches FR13_CAT10_BIND.md:65-66).

THE RESCUE FRACTION (the load-bearing number): d0-reject rate drops 0.1293 -> 0.0940, a reduction of 0.0353. As a fraction of cat9's root-rank-1 misses:
  rescue_rate = P(target == root-rank-2 | root-rank-1 missed) = (0.1293-0.0940)/0.1293 = 0.273.
So ~27% of the times the drafter's root rank-1 is NOT the verify-forward argmax, the root RANK-2 IS. Per boot this is ~21 d0 accepts saved (530 - 0.8707*585 = +20.6; raw aggregate delta 530-505 = +25 over +5 extra events).

CAVEAT (playbook class 12, measurement traps, line 17; class 9 engagement PASS, line 17): the streams diverge (served_lens cat9 [98,128,128,128] vs cat10 [73,128,128,128]), so 0.273 is a RATE over non-like-for-like trajectories, not a paired count. The clean paired number needs the deferred FR13_FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT GPU boot. 0.273 is the best CPU read and is a real, non-trivial hit rate (vs ~1/vocab if rank-2 were random) -> the rescue is genuine, not noise. No per-event rank-1/rank-2 margin dump was saved (FR13_CHASE_DIAG/caterpillar drafter trace were not enabled in these accept/speed boots), so 0.273 is the only direct quality signal.
reads.rootRank2Quality:
ROOT RANK-2 = A USEFUL CANDIDATE, NOT WASTED — but only on a minority of events (it is a near-tie 2nd, not a distant 2nd, in the cases that matter).

EVIDENCE it is useful: conditioned on root-rank-1 missing, the runner-up is the target 27.3% of the time. A distant/random 2nd would hit ~0%. 27% is a strong "2-horse-race" signature: when the drafter's top-1 is wrong at the root, it's usually wrong by a near-tie and the right token sits at rank-2. The root sibling captures exactly that.

TOKEN CHARACTER (inferred; root rank-2 token = topk(_fr10_logits,2).indices[:,1] off the SAME root logits, archive :9665-9667 / :9676-9679): the rescuable d0 positions are near-ties at the root. Corroborating from output/fr13_cat10/cat10/flips_vs_oracle.json: the clean teacher-forced argmax at decision points is frequently a low-confidence pick (clean_argmax_lp around -0.36/-0.43/-0.26/-0.21 at several flip positions, e.g. p2 pos27/28/36, p3 pos72/74/78/114/125) AND the served runner-up sits at small deviation (1.1-2.6 nat) — these are exactly the soft 2-way splits where a rank-2 token is the true argmax. (The other flip cluster — clean_argmax_lp near 0, deviation 8-17 nat — is the SEPARATE verify-forward defect, not a d0 near-tie.)

BUT it is wasted on the MAJORITY of events: root rank-1 already hits 87% of the time, and even among the 13% misses, 73% are NOT rank-2 either. So on ~96% of all events the (1,) row contributes nothing. That is the dilution source the bind reports (d1-d4 all down: -0.101/-0.074/-0.064/-0.063, BIND:67-69).
reads.costPerEvent:
COST PER EVENT = +1 verify row (node 1 = (1,) root leaf, slot 1 of the 10-node tree, archive packing :9994-10018), paid on 100% of events, while the rescue fires on only ~3.5% of events.

Direct speed cost (output/fr13_cat10/{cat9,cat10}/accept_speed.json):
  s_per_fwd 0.2258 -> 0.2287 = +0.0029s = +2.9 ms/fwd = 1.013x (the +1 lm-head GEMV row + GDN/conv co-residency over 10 vs 9 rows). This matches BIND:84 (predicted +1-row tax; ~+15ms/row is an upper bound, here ~3ms at B=1).
  warm decode TPS 18.40 -> 17.08 (-7.2%); per-req median 16.01 -> 15.17 (-5.3%) (BIND:81-82).

NET = rescue_benefit - cost is NEGATIVE:
  benefit = +0.0353 d0 accept/event.
  the +1 row is paid every event; the rescue only fires ~3.5% of events.
  AND the deeper-spine dilution (d1-d4) costs far more than d0 gains: total accept/event 3.1983 -> 2.9316 = -0.2667 (BIND:61-62). The +0.035 d0 gain is swamped by the -0.30 d1-d4 loss.
So cat10 as built loses on BOTH the per-row tax AND net accept; the d0 rescue is real but mispriced because the row is unconditional. (Whether the d1-d4 dilution is the +1-row verify co-residency [m1] or the branch-commit state handoff [m3] is the deferred FR13_FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT discriminator — this CPU read can't separate them, but it does establish the rescue itself is cheap in principle and only the UNCONDITIONAL row makes it expensive.)
reads.confidenceGatedIdea:
CONFIDENCE-GATED ROOT BRANCH (shape-true: still ONE single (1,) node, never deeper — honors the no-deepening ruling): emit the root sibling ONLY when the root is a near-tie; otherwise serve a clean cat9 9-node spine.

WHY it works: the entire 0.273 rescue lives in near-tie events (the 2-horse races). On confident-rank-1 events the runner-up is essentially never the target, so the (1,) row there is pure cost (extra row + the d1-d4 co-residency dilution) with ~0 rescue. Gate them out.

THE GATE (free to compute — no extra forward): at archive :9665, top2 = torch.topk(_fr10_logits, 2) is ALREADY materialized. Compute margin g = _fr10_logits[rank1] - _fr10_logits[rank2] (or a softmax-prob gap p1 - p2) and emit node (1,) only when g < tau (near-tie); else fall through to the cat9 caterpillar pack (:10020+). One scalar compare per event, zero added GEMV.

PAYOFF: the +1 verify row is paid only on the near-tie fraction of events (the only events where rescue is possible) instead of 100%, for ~the SAME ~21 d0 rescues. The confident-rank-1 events (the large majority) run as byte-identical cat9 — they keep the clean spine, so their d1-d4 are NOT diluted at all. Average row tax drops ~3-4x and the bulk of the -0.27 dilution disappears because most events never see the extra row.

CALIBRATION / CAVEATS: tau should be set from the actual root margin distribution at the d0-miss positions — which needs the FR13_CHASE_DIAG root-logit margin dump (not saved in these boots). Set tau so the near-tie bucket captures ~all rank-2 hits while excluding confident events; sweep on the deferred boot. Two things to verify post-22-flip: (1) the gate is variable-topology per event — confirm the verify packer + vLLM tree descriptor accept a per-event 9-or-10-node tree (engagement assert, class 9), and (2) re-run within-boot determinism (class 8) since the tree shape now depends on logits. This is the natural revisit AFTER the 22-flip fix: a clean spine plus a CHEAP, well-targeted d0 rescue for the 62%-of-greedy-rejects-at-step-0.

design.dilutionTiedTo22flip:
MAYBE — most likely PARTIALLY tied, but NOT fully, and the binding evidence says the two are largely SEPARATE phenomena that share one upstream cause (trajectory divergence), not one carrier.

THE CASE FOR "TIED" (the 22-flip and the -28 share the deep-verify co-residency, m1): both live on the SAME shipped replay-ON verify forward. The 22 clear-margin flips concentrate at the deep tree rows (node-7, depth 4-5; project_fr13_conv_priorwindow_root STATUS-2026-06-13: "STILL flips 22 vs native's 3 at node 7"), and the conditional decomposition I computed shows the dilution is NOT diffuse — it is a SINGLE sharp drop at the d0->d1 conditional transition (cat9 0.9505 -> cat10 0.8019, delta -0.1486; d1->d2 +0.0056, d2->d3 -0.0143, d3->d4 -0.0306, all near-flat; from output/fr13_cat10/{cat9,cat10}/metrics_final.txt per-pos [505,480,370,280,220] vs [530,425,330,245,185]). If the verify-forward's fp reduction-order / num_warps=8/BV=16 codegen seam (FR13_FLIP_DRAFTER_CAMPAIGN.md:20, the one un-closed GDN-scan seam vs native 4/BV=32) is what flips the 22 AND what perturbs the spine rows' accumulation when an extra real row sits in the 16-pad tile, then cleaning the spine to native-bit-exact would heal BOTH at once.

THE HARD EVIDENCE AGAINST "fully tied" (they are separate): the cat9 flip set and the cat10 flip set are 100% DISJOINT — I verified ZERO overlapping (prompt,pos) pairs. cat9 = {(0,69),(0,80),(0,82),(0,83),(0,84),(0,97),(1,50),(1,65),(1,67),(1,76),(1,115),(1,118),(2,21),(2,60),(2,92),(2,114),(3,61),(3,69),(3,73),(3,94),(3,101),(3,108)}; cat10 = {(0,58),(0,72),(1,64),(1,73),(1,74),(1,78),(1,83),(1,84),(2,27),(2,28),(2,36),(2,37),(2,84),(2,86),(2,121),(2,123),(3,68),(3,72),(3,74),(3,78),(3,114),(3,125)}; overlap = empty, 22 cat9-only + 22 cat10-only. The flip TOTAL is FLAT (22==22) but every single position MOVED. A shared single-carrier defect would pin flips to the same token contexts; instead the flips track the (different) greedy streams. The streams provably diverge early — cat10 p0 hit <|im_end|> EOS at 73 tokens vs cat9 at 98 (capture.json p0 last-3 toks both end ['\n','```','<|im_end|>'] but cat10 25 tokens sooner). So the 22-flip set is DOWNSTREAM of trajectory, and the redistribution is a trajectory artifact, not a shared mechanism.

VERDICT: fixing the 22-flip (driving the deep-verify spine rows to native-bit-exact) WILL remove the m1 component of the -28 (the residual fp-reduction perturbation of spine rows from the extra co-resident row) — and that is plausibly a real chunk of the d0->d1 -0.1486 drop. But it will NOT remove the m3 component (branch-commit handoff) NOR the trajectory/denominator confound (which the disjoint-flip evidence proves dominates the whole-window -0.27). So: the -28 SHRINKS after the 22-flip fix but does not vanish; the residual is m3 + the structural sibling-stop denominator effect. Net answer: MAYBE/partial — the verify-forward (m1) slice is the same carrier as the 22-flip; the rest is not. Only the post-fix re-run + FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT can quantify the split.
design.m3HandoffFix:
IF the residual dilution is m3 (branch-commit state handoff), the fix targets the conv-window + h0 state that the next event's rollout inherits when the root sibling WINS the commit.

THE MECHANISM in code (HEAD): the committer is LCP-max (fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:5620-5648, the best_lcp/best_path loop). The root sibling node (1,) is a leaf with parent=0; it can win ONLY when the spine's d0 (node 1) is rejected and the sibling matches d0 -> best_path=[0,2], best_lcp=1, a STOP-AT-d0 commit (accepted_len=1). When it wins, the next event's drafter rollout inherits state from the accepted path's LEAF NODE column: the conv prior-window is read from accepted_paths[b, len-1] at :1523-1538 (FR13_CONV_COMMITTED_PATH default-ON, "read from the accepted path's LEAF NODE column ... branch-winner-valid"), and h0 is the committed leaf's SSM state. On a sibling-stop the leaf is the OFF-SPINE node (1,)'s column, so the handoff seeds the next rollout from off-spine state.

WHY m3 IS BOUNDED-SMALL HERE (the key finding): a sibling commit has num_accepted=1. The documented conv prior-window defect (project_fr13_conv_priorwindow_root: wrong bank-row/cols, conv1d_out=18.375) fires at num_accepted>1 — it does NOT trigger on sibling-stops. So the most dangerous handoff channel is INERT for the ~5-rescue events/rep that actually go through the sibling. The realized rescue is small: d0 marginal 505->530 full-run (+25), 101->106 rep0 (+5); sibling-wins are a SUBSET of {events where spine-d0 missed}, so at most ~25 events ever take the sibling path. Their handoff cost is therefore tightly bounded.

THE FIX (only needed IF Boot 4 shows m3 is the residual carrier): on a sibling-stop commit, seed the NEXT event's conv prior-window and h0 from the ROOT (parent=0) state, NOT from the off-spine (1,) leaf column — i.e. treat a d0-only sibling commit as "advance one token, reset to the on-spine continuation state." Concretely: at :1523-1538, when accepted_paths[b, len-1] is the root-sibling leaf AND best_lcp==1, override h0_use_accepted_column to read the root's column (or recompute the 1-token advance from the spine root state) so the handoff is on-trajectory. This is a WIRING fix (which column the handoff reads), not a kernel rebuild — it changes the source row of the snapshot, exactly the class of fix the conv-committed-path block was built for. Verify gate: per-token argmax-vs-clean-oracle on the FIRST event AFTER each sibling-stop must match the no-sibling spine continuation (the handoff must not degrade the successor's d1-d4). Note: the confidence-gated design below makes most sibling rows never exist, which independently shrinks the m3 surface to near-zero, so the handoff fix may be moot once gating lands.
design.confidenceGatedPlan:
CONFIDENCE-GATED ROOT BRANCH — emit the (1,) root sibling row ONLY when the root is a near-tie; otherwise serve the clean cat9 9-node spine. Shape stays FIXED (caterpillar + at most ONE single root node, never deeper).

WHY it is the right lever: the entire 0.273 rescue lives in near-tie events. I measured the rescue fraction = P(target == root-rank-2 | root-rank-1 missed) = ((75/580)-(55/585))/(75/580) = 0.2729 — so when the drafter's root top-1 is wrong, the runner-up is the true token 27% of the time (a strong 2-horse-race signature vs ~0% for a random rank-2). But on confident-rank-1 events the runner-up is essentially never the target, so the (1,) row there is PURE cost: the +1 verify row (paid 100% of events as built) plus whatever m1/m3 dilution it carries, for ~0 rescue. Gate them out and the rescue stays while the cost collapses.

THE GATE (free — zero added forward): at the cat10 archive packing the root top-2 is ALREADY materialized via topk(root_logits, 2) (FR13_FLIP_DRAFTER_CAMPAIGN.md:9665-67, the rank-2 read). Compute the root margin g = root_logits[rank1] - root_logits[rank2] (or softmax-prob gap p1 - p2) and emit node (1,) only when g < tau (near-tie); else fall through to the cat9 caterpillar pack. One scalar compare per event, no extra GEMV, no extra lm-head row on confident events.

PAYOFF: the +1 verify row (and its co-residency dilution) is paid only on the near-tie fraction of events instead of 100%, for ~the same ~21 d0 rescues/boot. Confident-rank-1 events (the large majority) run byte-identical to cat9 — their d1-d4 are NOT diluted at all, so the bulk of the -0.27 disappears mechanically (most events never see the extra row). The s/fwd tax (cat10 0.2287 vs cat9 0.2258 = +2.9ms, +1.3%, output/fr13_cat10 accept_speed.json) drops ~3-4x to its near-tie-weighted average.

CALIBRATION + ENGAGEMENT CAVEATS: tau must be set from the actual root-margin distribution at the d0-miss positions, which needs the FR13_CHASE_DIAG root-logit-margin dump (NOT saved in these boots — capture.json holds only served streams). Sweep tau on the post-fix boot so the near-tie bucket captures ~all rank-2 hits while excluding confident events. Two NEW gates because the topology is now per-event variable: (1) class 9 engagement — confirm the verify packer + vLLM tree descriptor accept a per-event 9-OR-10-node tree (the cat10 packer assumed a fixed 10-node tree; variable n_actual/n_pad must be asserted, and n_pad already rounds 9->16 and 10->16 so the pad tile is unchanged); (2) class 8 within-boot determinism — re-run rep1==rep2 byte-identical since the tree SHAPE now depends on logits (a new determinism surface). This gating is the natural post-22-flip revisit: a clean spine + a CHEAP, well-targeted d0 rescue.
design.decisiveGpuTestPostFix:
RUN ORDER (after the 22-flip spine fix lands, ONE GPU, serialized, recover_host_memory + free-g between boots, class 8 det + class 9 engagement first-gates on every boot, all eager B=1 greedy seed 1313 on output/fr13_acceptance_ladder/prompts_swe4.json, plus a temp-0.6 superset pass; replay-ON shipped path):

BOOT A — re-run cat9 (control) on the FIXED spine. Confirm the 22 flips dropped to ~native 3 and re-measure accept/event (expect it to RISE toward native 3.076-3.16 as the deep-row defect clears). This is the new clean baseline — the dilution must be measured against THIS, not the old cat9 3.198.

BOOT B — re-run cat10 (FR13_CAT10_ROOT_SIBLING=1) on the FIXED spine, FULL verify tree, normal LCP commit. Measure accept/event + the d0->d1 conditional. OUTCOME READ: if the d0->d1 conditional drop (was -0.1486 cat9->cat10) SHRINKS toward 0 -> the dilution was m1 (verify-forward co-residency) and the 22-flip fix healed it (the -28 and the 22-flip were the same carrier). If the d0->d1 drop PERSISTS -> the residual is m3 or trajectory.

BOOT C — the DECISIVE m1-vs-m3 discriminator: cat10 + FR13_FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT=1 (fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:5582/:5673, commits the spine path's own LCP, full 10-row verify tree STILL runs but the sibling can NEVER win the commit -> m3 handoff is neutralized, m1 co-residency is still live). OUTCOMES: (i) deep-spine accept RECOVERS to BOOT-A cat9 level => the residual dilution was m3 (branch-commit handoff) -> apply the m3HandoffFix; (ii) deep-spine accept STILL diluted vs BOOT A => the residual is m1 (the extra real row perturbs the spine's fp accumulation in the 16-pad tile even when it never commits) -> the 22-flip fix did NOT fully cover the co-residency channel, and the gate is the only way to avoid paying it; (iii) BOOT B already clean (no residual after the spine fix) => FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT is confirmatory and the unconditional cat10 may already net-win.

BOOT D — the confidence-gated cat10 (tau-swept). Measure net accept/event and TPS vs BOOT-A cat9 and vs native E5. This is the SHIP candidate.

KEY SUBTLETY: the saved per-event winner/bonus_source log (the FR10_METRICS jsonl + committer bonus_source 'reject_parent_target'/'tree_self_target') was NOT persisted to output/fr13_cat10/ (capture.json = served streams only; launch.log = a 4-line free -g snapshot) — so the count of root-sibling-commit events CANNOT be read from the saved data. Boots B-D MUST enable FR10_METRICS=1 + the bonus_source log so each sibling-commit event is counted and its successor event's d1-d4 can be checked for handoff degradation (the direct m3 test the CPU pass cannot do).
design.expectedNetAccept:
EXPECTED NET ACCEPT — the root branch likely TIES or marginally BEATS native at d0 in expectation but the WHOLE-WINDOW superset verdict is NOT guaranteed and must be measured at temp>0; at greedy it is capped.

THE GREEDY CEILING: at greedy a lossless tree = the unique native argmax chain, so accept/event is CAPPED at native MTP-5 = 3.076 (FR13_DECISIVE_TEST.md: "branches give NO lossless greedy speedup"). The root branch's ONLY greedy contribution is the d0 rescue: it converts a d0-reject into a d0-accept when target==root-rank-2 (the user-confirmed GREEDY branch rescue 86a255a4 — at greedy the sibling-commit-through is a legitimate +1 d0 accept). So at greedy the gated cat10 can push d0 accept rate above cat9's spine-only d0 rate (0.871 -> ~0.906, +0.035) WITHOUT the d1-d4 dilution (gating removes the unconditional row), landing accept/event at roughly cat9-clean + the d0 rescue increment, i.e. approaching but not exceeding the 3.076 native greedy cap unless the spine-fix itself lifts cat9 past native.

THE QUANTITATIVE EXPECTATION: post-22-flip clean cat9 should land near native (~3.08-3.16 accept/event, the documented native self-floor spread). The gated d0 rescue adds ~+0.035 d0 accept/event on the near-tie events at ~3.5% of the +1-row cost (vs cat10's unconditional 1.3% s/fwd tax on 100% of events). NET at greedy: gated-cat10 accept/event = clean-cat9 + ~0.02-0.04 (the realized rescue, slightly below +0.035 because gating may miss a few rank-2 hits at the tau boundary), MINUS a near-tie-weighted row tax that is ~3-4x smaller than cat10's 1.3%. So at GREEDY the gated root branch is expected to be a SMALL NET WIN over clean-cat9 on accept and roughly TPS-neutral — and it BEATS native iff clean-cat9 already matches native and the rescue increment is not eaten by the residual tax. It does NOT clear a STRICT superset-over-native bar on accept ALONE at greedy (capped at the chain).

THE REAL SUPERSET WIN IS TEMP>0: the no-copy tree's superset speedup is a temp>0 phenomenon (rejection-sampling accepts multiple candidates losslessly; FR13_DECISIVE_TEST.md). The root sibling gives a SECOND root candidate, which at temp 0.6 is exactly where an extra accepted root token shows up. So the binding "does it BEAT native" test is the temp-0.6 superset pass (accept/event >= 3.076 + bag-TV within self-noise floor <= 0.0593), measured against BOOT-A clean-cat9 and native E5 — NOT the greedy whole-window number (which the BIND already flagged as a trajectory-confounded DRAW). HONEST BOTTOM LINE: expect gated-cat10 to be a small net-positive at greedy and the candidate to BEAT native at temp>0 IF the spine fix makes the deep rows lossless; but the whole-window superset verdict requires the post-fix boots — the CPU data cannot promise it.
design.summary:
CPU read of output/fr13_cat10/{cat9,cat10}/{accept_speed.json,metrics_final.txt,flips_vs_oracle.json,capture.json} + FR13_CAT10_BIND.md + FR13_FLIP_DRAFTER_CAMPAIGN.md + the archived committer/handoff/gate code (fr13-cat10-archive @ 986c6e77; HEAD seams at fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py :1523-1538 conv-committed-path handoff, :5582/:5673 FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT, :4108-4118 replay/store_node_states, :827 conv-fused-requires-replay).

WHAT THE -28 ACTUALLY IS (mechanism rank, resolving the paradox): the drafter FORWARD is byte-identical cat9-vs-cat10 (the root sibling is a rank-2 READ never fed forward, only woven into the verify PACKING ORDER), so the -0.2667 (3.1983->2.9316) is VERIFY-side, not drafter co-residency. RANK 1 = trajectory/denominator ARTIFACT (dominant): the two arms produce DIFFERENT greedy streams that diverge early (cat10 p0 EOS'd at 73 tokens vs cat9 98; cat10 made 25 fewer tokens in 1 more event, mechanically lowering accept/event); the conditional decomposition I computed shows the dilution is NOT diffuse but a SINGLE sharp drop at the d0->d1 conditional (cat9 0.9505 -> cat10 0.8019, -0.1486; d1->d2/d2->d3/d3->d4 all near-flat), and the cat9/cat10 flip sets are 100% DISJOINT (zero overlapping (prompt,pos) pairs, 22 each) -> flip redistribution is trajectory-driven, NOT a shared carrier. RANK 2 = m3 branch-commit handoff (real but bounded-small: sibling-stops are accepted_len=1 so the num_accepted>1 conv prior-window bug stays inert; only ~5 rescue events/rep). RANK 3 = m1 verify-forward co-residency (structurally weakened: strict_mask makes the (1,) row attention/scan-invisible to every spine row; residual = sub-ULP fp-reduction in the shared 16-pad tile only).

THE PLAN: (1) dilution-vs-22-flip = MAYBE/partial — the m1 slice shares the deep-verify carrier with the 22-flip and should heal with the spine fix, but the disjoint-flip evidence proves the bulk is trajectory + m3, so the -28 shrinks not vanishes. (2) m3 fix = on a sibling-stop, seed the next event's conv-window/h0 from the ROOT column not the off-spine (1,) leaf (a wiring change at :1523-1538), only if Boot C shows m3 is the residual. (3) Confidence-gated root branch = emit (1,) ONLY when root margin g<tau (near-tie; the gate is free, root top-2 already materialized), paying the +1 row on ~the near-tie fraction not 100% for the same ~21 d0 rescues (rescue fraction 0.2729) -> removes most of the -0.27. (4) Decisive post-fix GPU test = re-run clean cat9 (new baseline) + cat10 + cat10+FR13_FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT (the m1-vs-m3 discriminator: recover=>m3, persist=>m1) + gated-cat10, WITH FR10_METRICS=1 to count sibling commits (NOT in saved data). Expected net: small greedy win over clean-cat9 (capped at native 3.076 chain), real superset-beats-native only at temp 0.6 IF the spine fix makes deep rows lossless — must be measured, not promised. KEY DATA LIMIT: no per-event winner/bonus_source log was persisted, so root-sibling-commit count and handoff-degradation cannot be confirmed from CPU; requires the post-fix boots.

cat10Verify.dilutionRealOrArtifact: ARTIFACT-DOMINATED. A sibling rescue commits the 2-node path [0,2] then STOPS, swelling per_pos[0] (the d1|d0 denominator) but unable to reach pos 2,3,4. Conditional decomp is a SINGLE sharp d0->d1 drop (cat9 0.9505 -> cat10 0.8019, delta -0.1486; d2|d1 +0.0057, d3|d2 -0.0144, d4|d3 -0.0306 near-flat); that exact single-spike signature IS the depth-cap artifact, NOT spine dilution. The load-bearing unknown: once the sibling-stop depth-cap artifact is stripped (only the per-node counter can isolate it; it is ABSENT from every saved file, confirmed by grep showing only per_pos), is there ANY residual spine d1-d4 dilution? cat10Verify.issues: holds=FALSE. Material problems: (1) WRONG INTERPRETATION OF d0->d1 DROP (most important): DESIGN (dilutionTiedTo22flip) and MECHANISM frame the single sharp d0->d1 -0.1486 as the m1 verify-forward dilution carrier. It is NOT; it is the signature of the sibling-stop depth-cap DENOMINATOR artifact (sibling leaf [0,2] swells per_pos[0], cannot reach pos2-4). I reproduced the conditional decomp (cat9 [0.8707,0.9505,0.7708,0.7568,0.7857] vs cat10 [0.906,0.8019,0.7765,0.7424,0.7551]) and showed de-confounding pos0 recovers d1|d0 to ~0.84+. DESIGN cites the same numbers but draws the OPPOSITE conclusion. (2) The DESIGN's own disjoint-flip evidence (independently verified: 0 overlap, exact sets match BIND [6,6,4,6]/[2,6,8,6]) REFUTES 'tied to 22-flip', yet dilutionTiedTo22flip still concludes 'MAYBE/partial, the m1 slice IS the same carrier'. Given (1)+(2) the m1-tied component is plausibly ~zero; the tie claim is largely wishful. (3) d0-rescue fraction 0.2729 (confidenceGatedPlan) is presented as measured P(target==rank2|rank1 missed); it is a CROSS-ARM inference over two DIFFERENT trajectories (580 vs 585 events), confounded; no saved per-node sibling-win counter. (4) confidenceGatedPlan understates a real obstacle: it claims 'one scalar compare per event, no extra GEMV' saves the +1 verify row on confident events, but topology (strict_mask/parent/n_pad/replay matrix) is built ONCE from static tree_choices (archive L216-242; is_caterpillar10 asserts tree_choices_current==cat10_choices for the whole boot). A per-event variable 9-OR-10-node tree is NOT supported; the row-cost-saving payoff needs variable topology, a substantial change. The proposal IS shape-true (caterpillar + <=1 root node, no deepening) and lossless-safe (committed tokens stay verify-validated); only the cost claim is overstated. (5) The decisive GPU test (FORCE_SPINE_COMMIT) IS decisive for m1-vs-m3 but INSUFFICIENT alone: it cannot de-confound the depth-cap denominator artifact, which dominates; must pair with a per-node sibling-vs-spine d0 counter. NON-ISSUES (verified correct): the paradox premise is CORRECT, the drafter forward is byte-identical cat9-vs-cat10 (root sibling = topk(root_logits,2).indices[:,1] rank-2 READ, never fed to spine rollout, only a pack slot; archive L9665-67,9994-10024). No reward-hacks in any proposal. Speed numbers reproduce (s/fwd 0.2258/0.2287, ratio 1.013, +2.94ms; warm TPS 18.40/17.08).
